Subject: Post-demo qualification: deployment & migration next steps

Thanks again for your time earlier — appreciated the clear questions from the product and infra teams. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

High-level recap:
- Use case: conversational assistant + document extraction for support workflows (PII in a subset of requests).
- Current footprint: mix of OpenAI-hosted calls for public data + an on-prem GPU cluster used for sensitive processing.
- Goals: p95 latency <= 200ms, predictable unit cost, and clear auditability for sensitive traffic.

Options that make sense given the call (short):
1) Hosted API: fastest to ship; easiest procurement; good for non-sensitive traffic; we can apply token limits & caching to meet cost targets.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool (SLA-backed) — good when you need predictable throughput and lower per-token cost for steady volume.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): for regulatory/strict data residency — requires longer lead time and network setup.

Open questions / asks for you (please reply inline):
- Traffic shape: typical RPS/QPS and peak concurrency (we heard ~100–150/min peak; please confirm).
- Token profile: average prompt + generation tokens per request (approx).
- Migration sources: are you planning to lift-and-shift from OpenAI API only, or also migrate models running on your on-prem GPU cluster?
- Data residency: which endpoints must stay on-prem / in VPC?
- SLA needs: specific uptime/penalty requirements?

Next steps I propose:
- You + infra: confirm the numeric answers above.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical workshop (our infra + your SREs) to walk through network/firewall and routing for hybrid flows.
- I’ll share a short one-pager with deploy option tradeoffs and a Dedicated sizing estimate.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-options-onepager.pdf, dedicated-sizing-estimate.xlsx (high-level numbers).

If it helps, I can sketch two recommended paths based on your answers: (A) PoC on Hosted + parallel Dedicated provisioning for sensitive lanes, or (B) Dedicated-first if you want to avoid any external API for production.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Inline answers below and a few clarifying questions from our side.

Inline: 
- Traffic shape: average ~45 req/min during business hours; peak occasional bursts up to ~180 requests/min for batch ticket uploads. Concurrency usually stays low (1–3 concurrent per user).
- Token profile: average request ~120 tokens prompt + ~80 tokens generation (~200 tokens total).
- Migration sources: currently we call OpenAI for most low-risk traffic. We also run custom fine-tuned models on a legacy on-prem cluster (NVIDIA A100 nodes) that process PII-heavy requests — those must remain under our control unless very strong contractual guarantees are in place.
- Data residency: PII processing must remain on-prem. Non-PII can go to cloud (hosted or dedicated).
- SLA needs: targeting 99.9% uptime for production flows; open to commercial SLA language.

Questions for Redwood: 
- Can you support hybrid routing so we can continue to send PII requests to our cluster and route everything else to Redwood Dedicated/Hosted? Any added latency for dual-routing?
- For Dedicated, what is the expected lead time to provision an initial pool sized for ~200 req/min and p95 <200ms?
- We’ll need SOC 2 report and a short security questionnaire answered for our procurement team (I can attach their template).

We’re leaning toward a Dedicated-first approach for production because of compliance, but would like a short PoC on Hosted for feature validation if provisioning time is long.

Attaching procurement questionnaire (separate email if needed).

—Maya

Maya — great, thanks for the fast answers and the clear constraints. Short responses and a recommended migration pattern below.

Hybrid routing and latency:
- Yes — Redwood supports policy-based routing. You can keep PII requests routed to your on-prem cluster (we do this via a secure VPC peering + a routing policy at the edge) and send non-sensitive traffic to Dedicated or Hosted. Typical added latency for routing decisions is <10ms; the main delta will be the network hop to your cluster.

Dedicated provisioning lead time:
- Initial Reserved pool for the size you listed (capacity to sustain ~200 req/min at p95 <200ms) is typically 3–4 weeks to provision from order to green/healthy (includes capacity allocation and verification). Can be faster with a committed start date.

Recommended migration path (proposed):
1) Short Hosted PoC (2–4 weeks): validate prompts, prompt-sets, and local evals against your golden-set. Non-PII only.
2) Stand up Dedicated pool in parallel (3–4 week lead). Configure canary routing so a subset of traffic (non-PII) shifts to Dedicated for cost/latency baseline.
3) Hybrid routing cutover for PII: route PII to your on-prem cluster (no model movement required) and non-PII to Dedicated once validated.

Deliverables we’ll share this week:
- migration-playbook-v0.2.docx (high-level steps, rollback plan)
- redwood-sla-draft-1.0.pdf (SLA language you can use in procurement)
- short SOC 2 summary + pointer to longer audit pack (we’ll send via secure Drive link)

Can we schedule the technical workshop next Thu or Fri? Karthik (cc’d) will join for sizing. Also looping in Prioy (cc’d) from our onboarding team to prepare the Dedicated quote.

Thanks — Jordan
